html:
Kaminaljuyu was a large Maya city in the highlands of Guatemala, on the site of today's Guatemala City. It was inhabited for well over two thousand years and was at its height between about 400 BCE and 100 CE.

It controlled nearby sources of obsidian, the volcanic glass used for blades, and fed its people with canals drawn from a lake. Its carved monuments carry some of the earliest Maya writing. Around 400 CE it took on many features of Teotihuacan in central Mexico, at the same time as Teotihuacan's intervention at Tikal.

Most of its hundreds of mounds have been destroyed as Guatemala City spread over them, and only a small park remains. It shows that the Maya highlands were as old and important as the lowland cities of Guatemala.
sum: Kaminaljuyu was a large Maya city in the highlands of Guatemala, on the site of today's Guatemala City. It was inhabited for well over two thousand years and was at its height between about 400 BCE and 100 CE.
